title: Should we pay more for chocolate?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: the process of cutting down trees
a farm owned by its workers
a business that wants to help the community

keywords.term: to trace something back to something
keywords.def: to find out where something has come from
data taken from a device which can show you exactly where a person or thing is
at a large distance from places where other people live

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. How many of our listeners, Neil, do you think love chocolate?
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Becca。Neil，你觉得我们的听众里有多少人喜欢巧克力？

sentences.en: Well, I can't think of anyone who doesn't love chocolate.
sentences.zh: 额，我想不出有谁是不喜欢巧克力的。

sentences.en: I know, I certainly do. Yes, I thought you might say that, having seen your mid-morning snack most days!
sentences.zh: 我知道，我肯定喜欢。是的，我猜你就会这么说，毕竟我几乎每天上午都能看到你吃巧克力当零食！

sentences.en: That's true. I do love a bit of dark chocolate.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。我确实很喜欢吃点黑巧克力。

sentences.en: Do you know, I really like the one that's got some chilli in it.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我真的很喜欢那种带点辣椒味的巧克力。

sentences.en: What's your favourite, Becca? Oh, I also love dark chocolate, but chilli is a bit spicy for me.
sentences.zh: 你最喜欢哪种，Becca？哦，我也喜欢黑巧克力，但辣椒对我来说有点太辣了。

sentences.en: I like it with sea salt. Hmm, that's also good.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢加了海盐的。嗯，那也很不错。

sentences.en: But now to the stuff that makes chocolate possible - cocoa - a key ingredient and it's become more expensive in recent years.
sentences.zh: 但现在让我们来谈谈制作巧克力的原料——可可——这是一种关键成分，而且近年来变得越来越贵了。

sentences.en: Now, a new EU law could make chocolate even more expensive.
sentences.zh: 现在，一项新的欧盟法律可能会让巧克力变得更加昂贵。

sentences.en: Today, we'll talk about how this law could change things for farmers, companies and chocolate lovers, as discussed on the recent BBC World Service programme Business Daily.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将讨论这项法律可能会给农民、公司和巧克力爱好者带来怎样的改变，正如最近 BBC World Service 的节目 Business Daily 中所讨论的那样。

sentences.en: As always, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases and you'll find all the vocabulary along with a transcript on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们将学习一些实用的新单词和短语，您可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇以及文本转写。

sentences.en: Before we get started Neil, I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，Neil，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: Europeans are big fans of chocolate, just like us!
sentences.zh: 欧洲人非常喜欢巧克力，就像我们一样！

sentences.en: Around how many tonnes of cocoa beans were imported to Europe in 2023?
sentences.zh: 2023年大约有多少吨可可豆进口到欧洲？

sentences.en: Was it: a) 500,000 tonnes b) two million tonnes c) 10 million tonnes Well, I have no idea, but I'm just going to guess and say 500,000 tonnes.
sentences.zh: 是：a) 50万吨 b) 200万吨 还是 c) 1000万吨？额，我完全不知道，但我打算瞎猜一个，选 50万吨。

sentences.en: We'll find out if you're right later on!
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会看看你是否答对了！

sentences.en: Now, that new EU law that we were talking about earlier would stop companies buying cocoa from land where any trees were cut down in the last six years.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们之前提到的那项新欧盟法律将禁止公司从过去六年内砍伐过树木的土地上购买可可。

sentences.en: The process of cutting down trees is called deforestation.
sentences.zh: 砍伐树木的过程被称为森林砍伐（deforestation）。

sentences.en: Albert Smith, who owns a small chocolate business, believes that the new law wouldn't change too much for his company.
sentences.zh: 经营着一家小型巧克力公司的 Albert Smith 认为，这项新法律对他的公司不会有太大改变。

sentences.en: …we have all the information on farm level already because the producers that we work with are small plantations that either work through a co-op or social enterprise and all of our cocoa is already traced back to the plantation.
sentences.zh: “……我们已经掌握了农场层面的所有信息，因为与我们合作的生产者都是小型种植园，他们要么通过合作社运作，要么通过社会企业运作，而且我们所有的可可都已经可以追溯到种植园了。”

sentences.en: Albert adds that they already know where the cocoa beans come from, as they work with farmers from co-ops or social enterprises.
sentences.zh: Albert 补充说，他们已经知道可可豆来自哪里，因为他们与来自合作社或社会企业的农民合作。

sentences.en: A co-op in this case is a farm owned by its workers.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，合作社（co-op）是指由其工人共同拥有的农场。

sentences.en: A social enterprise is a business that wants to help the community.
sentences.zh: 社会企业（social enterprise）是指旨在帮助社区的企业。

sentences.en: Because of working with farmers who are part of these organisations, Albert says that the cocoa they buy can already be traced back to the farms.
sentences.zh: Albert 表示，由于与这些组织的农民合作，他们购买的可可已经可以追溯到农场。

sentences.en: To trace something back to something, means to find out where something has come from.
sentences.zh: 将某物追溯到某处（trace something back to something），意思是找出某物的来源。

sentences.en: Here’s Albert Smith again. Mapping means that farmers have to actually provide the geolocations of their plantation.
sentences.zh: 下面再次请出 Albert Smith。测绘意味着农民实际上必须提供他们种植园的地理定位。

sentences.en: And you know, for some farmers that are very remote, that comes also with a challenge.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，对于一些非常偏远的农民来说，这也带来了一个挑战。

sentences.en: Albert suggests that giving a geolocation is difficult for some farmers, as they live in remote places and don't all have mobile phones.
sentences.zh: Albert 指出，提供地理定位对一些农民来说很困难，因为他们住在偏远的地方，而且并不是所有人都有手机。

sentences.en: Geolocation is data taken from a special device which shows exactly where something is, and the term remote means at a large distance from places where other people live.
sentences.zh: 地理定位（geolocation）是从特殊设备获取的数据，用于精确显示某物的位置；而“偏远”（remote）一词的意思是距离其他人居住的地方非常遥远。

sentences.en: Because of these changes, the price of chocolate might go up even more, meaning that chocolate lovers us could really notice the difference in our bank accounts.
sentences.zh: 由于这些变化，巧克力的价格可能会进一步上涨，这意味着我们这些巧克力爱好者可能会在银行账户上明显感受到这种变化。

sentences.en: Reporter, Matthew Kenyon, asked a chocolate lover on the street if they would pay more for their chocolate.
sentences.zh: 记者 Matthew Kenyon 在街上询问了一位巧克力爱好者，问他们是否愿意为巧克力支付更多的钱。

sentences.en: Chocolate Lover 1 Absolutely I would do that because I think the normal chocolates are way too cheap.
sentences.zh: 巧克力爱好者 1：绝对愿意，因为我觉得普通的巧克力太便宜了。

sentences.en: Definitely we will pay, we have to pay more because the money will go to the local people, to give them a better life, also to tackle deforestation.
sentences.zh: 我们肯定会付，也必须付更多的钱，因为这些钱会流向当地人，让他们过上更好的生活，同时也能解决森林砍伐问题。

sentences.en: And he asked another chocolate lover about whether he looks at where the cocoa beans come from.
sentences.zh: 他还询问了另一位巧克力爱好者，问他是否会关注可可豆的来源。

sentences.en: Chocolate Lover 2 For me, personally, absolutely not!
sentences.zh: 巧克力爱好者 2：对我个人而言，绝对不会！

sentences.en: Out of principle, because I want them to be produced most efficiently as possible.
sentences.zh: 出于原则，因为我希望它们的生产效率尽可能高。

sentences.en: The cost is completely irrelevant. But on principle, I want production to be as efficient as possible.
sentences.zh: 成本完全无关紧要。但原则上，我希望生产尽可能高效。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it's a waste of everybody's time.
sentences.zh: 否则，那就是在浪费大家的时间。

sentences.en: Mixed opinions, it seems there Becca! Whilst one chocolate lover would pay more for chocolate to support farmers and production, the other doesn't worry too much about the cost, but says the production process should be as efficient as possible.
sentences.zh: 看来大家的意见不一，Becca！虽然一位巧克力爱好者愿意为巧克力支付更多费用以支持农民和生产，但另一位并不太担心成本，而是认为生产过程应该尽可能高效。

sentences.en: OK, time to answer our quiz question. Earlier, I asked you how many tonnes of cocoa were imported to Europe in 2023 and you said 500,000 tonnes.
sentences.zh: 好了，是时候回答我们的测验问题了。之前，我问你 2023 年有多少吨可可进口到欧洲，你说是 50 万吨。

sentences.en: Well, Neil, I'll tell you, it is 2 million tonnes!
sentences.zh: 好吧，Neil，我告诉你，是 200 万吨！

sentences.en: Wow. Well, I was wrong and that really is a lot.
sentences.zh: 哇。好吧，我猜错了，那确实非常多。

sentences.en: Between us, we've probably eaten a few tonnes already this year!
sentences.zh: 我们俩今年可能已经吃掉了好几吨了！

sentences.en: At least, Becca! I'd be interested to know what kind of chocolate our listeners enjoy!
sentences.zh: 至少有这么多，Becca！我很想知道我们的听众喜欢什么种类的巧克力！

sentences.en: Me too! And whether they would be happy about paying more for their favourite chocolate bar!
sentences.zh: 我也是！还有他们是否愿意为自己最喜欢的巧克力棒支付更多的钱！

sentences.en: OK, let's recap some of the vocabulary from today.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们复习一下今天学到的一些词汇。

sentences.en: Deforestation is the process of cutting down trees.
sentences.zh: 森林砍伐（deforestation）是指砍伐树木的过程。

sentences.en: We heard co-op which is a farm owned by its workers.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了合作社（co-op），这是一种由其工人共同拥有的农场。

sentences.en: A social enterprise is a business that wants to help the community.
sentences.zh: 社会企业（social enterprise）是指旨在帮助社区的企业。

sentences.en: To trace something back to something is to find out where something has come from.
sentences.zh: 将某物追溯到某处（trace something back to something）是指找出某物的来源。

sentences.en: Geolocation is data taken from a device which can show you exactly where a person or thing is.
sentences.zh: 地理定位（geolocation）是从设备中获取的数据，可以精确显示人或物的位置。

sentences.en: And finally, remote means at a large distance from places where other people live.
sentences.zh: 最后，偏远（remote）的意思是距离其他人居住的地方非常遥远。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you want to test your knowledge, visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you'll also find a worksheet and quiz for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但如果你想测试一下自己的知识，请访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，你还可以在那里找到本期节目的工作单和测验。

sentences.en: Bye! See you next time. Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！下次见。再见！
